page: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a general-purpose bare-metal server utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, delivering 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system features 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier (top 10%) performance in multi-core CPU execution, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is also in the top 10% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes. The server demonstrates strong (top 25%) single-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests. In application-specific benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier throughput for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation with Clang. Large language model (LLM) inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds across 135M, 7B, and 70B models, though text generation speeds drop to average (middle 50%) for 135M and 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.metal-48xl provides high resource density with dedicated physical cores and high-speed DDR5 memory, making it suitable for workloads requiring bare-metal access without hypervisor overhead. However, the lack of bundled local storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a tradeoff, requiring external network storage and limiting its utility for hardware-accelerated deep learning training. It is best suited for large-scale general-purpose workloads, high-throughput database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
